title: The goal form's risk class becomes a policy tier, and the live dispatch carries the opt-ins it earns
description:
SPIDR child A of parent task-d56a0cc5f6ae4dc88da5233a9702d9e6 ("One approval, then unattended"), split 2026-09-09 by architect-fa84777a after measuring the parent at ~20 files across three packages against a 10-file cap. This is the DEPENDENCY LEAF: rows B (Gate 2) and C (Gate 3) both consume the mapping and the carried opt-ins, and both declare dependsOn on this row. Plan and land this FIRST.

OWNER DIRECTION driving the parent (2026-09-09): "we dont want moe-next to be stuck all the time for user approval we can approve the plan at the start but thats it". One human gate at plan/contract time; the rest unattended, with a human ABLE to intervene but not REQUIRED.

MEASURED AT HEAD 2026-09-09 by architect-fa84777a. Re-measure before planning; these are the facts this row is scoped against:
- `git grep -n "autoApprovalOptIns" -- packages/** apps/** adapters/**`: the ONLY production caller is apps/control-room/src/live/live-dispatch-payloads.ts:100 `autoApprovalOptIns: [], riskClassifications: RISK_CLASSIFICATIONS, rules: [],`. Every other hit is a fixture or a .test file. RISK_CLASSIFICATIONS is a local const at :31-36 carrying four `{factId, tier}` entries (R1/R0/R0/R2).
- `git grep -n "AdvisoryRiskClass" -- apps/**`: goal-model.ts:90 `export type AdvisoryRiskClass = "STANDARD" | "ELEVATED" | "RESTRICTED";`, optional field at goal-model.ts:124, set at new-goal-form.tsx:55 and :215. Consumed ONLY at apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/live-goal-create.ts in briefOfDraft as `lines.push(`Risk class: ${draft.riskClass}`)` - a line of PROSE in the brief. No mapping to R0..R3 exists anywhere.
- DEPENDENCY EDGE VERIFIED, no manifest edit needed: apps/control-room/package.json declares `"@moe/core": "workspace:*"`; pnpm-lock.yaml carries the `apps/control-room:` importer at line 70; production code already imports the bare specifier (apps/control-room/src/approvals/approval-gating.ts:4 `} from "@moe/core";`).
- BARREL EXPORTS CONFIRMED at packages/core/src/policy/policy-public.ts: POLICY_AUTO_APPROVAL_TIERS (:40), POLICY_RISK_TIERS (:45), type PolicyRiskTier (:63).
- TYPE-LEVEL FENCE, load-bearing for this row: policy-contract.ts:90-93 `interface PolicyAutoApprovalOptIn { readonly action: string; readonly tier: PolicyAutoApprovalTier }` and :28 `POLICY_AUTO_APPROVAL_TIERS = ["R0","R1"]`. An opt-in CANNOT carry R2 or R3 - the compiler refuses it. So a RESTRICTED goal yields NO opt-in by construction, not by a runtime check this row writes.

OWNER RULING 2026-09-09 on the mapping arithmetic. The parent's DoD asked for set equality both directions between 3 AdvisoryRiskClass values and 4 POLICY_RISK_TIERS, which no total function can satisfy (a 3-set cannot surject onto a 4-set). The owner chose: drop the reachability half, keep totality and injectivity. THE MAPPING IS EXACTLY:
  STANDARD   -> R0  (auto-approvable)
  ELEVATED   -> R1  (auto-approvable)
  RESTRICTED -> R3  (human-only)
R2 is deliberately unreachable from the form. Nothing is weakened: R2 and R3 are both human-only at policy-evaluation.ts:155-158, which returns REQUIRE_HUMAN_APPROVAL with code HUMAN_ONLY_TIER for both. Do NOT add a fourth advisory class and do NOT widen POLICY_AUTO_APPROVAL_TIERS.

WHAT THIS ROW DOES, and nothing more. One typed total mapping from AdvisoryRiskClass to PolicyRiskTier, in its own small module under apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/. Then live-dispatch-payloads.ts stops passing `autoApprovalOptIns: []` unconditionally: it derives the opt-in list from the goal draft's risk class, emitting opt-ins for the two gate actions ONLY when the mapped tier is in POLICY_AUTO_APPROVAL_TIERS, and an empty list otherwise. The risk class stops being only prose; leave the existing brief line in place (it is advisory text the operator reads) and ADD the typed path beside it.

OUT OF SCOPE, owned by sibling rows - do not touch these files: no daemon change of any kind; no preview or release edge; no decision-record shape; no digest mirror rotation; no MCP allowlist edit; no change to POLICY_AUTO_APPROVAL_TIERS or POLICY_RISK_TIERS.

The action strings the opt-ins name must be MEASURED from the kind constants, not invented: preview-contracts.ts:43 `PREVIEW_DECIDE_COMMAND_KIND = "preview.decide"` and release-decide-contracts.ts for RELEASE_DECIDE_COMMAND_KIND. Grep them; do not hand-type a literal that drifts.
definitionOfDone: A typed total mapping from AdvisoryRiskClass to PolicyRiskTier exists in one module under apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/, with an arm that asserts it is TOTAL (every value in a literal ['STANDARD','ELEVATED','RESTRICTED'] roster maps) and INJECTIVE (three distinct tiers), and pins the three pairs exactly: STANDARD->R0, ELEVATED->R1, RESTRICTED->R3. The arm iterates a roster declared in the TEST, not the mapping's own keys, so deleting a mapping entry goes RED.

An arm asserts the mapping is closed against the production tier vocabulary: every mapped tier is a member of POLICY_RISK_TIERS imported from the @moe/core bare specifier, and the two auto-approvable results (R0, R1) are members of POLICY_AUTO_APPROVAL_TIERS while R3 is NOT. Assert membership against the imported constants, never against re-typed string literals.

apps/control-room/src/live/live-dispatch-payloads.ts no longer contains the literal `autoApprovalOptIns: []` as an unconditional value; `git grep -n 'autoApprovalOptIns: \[\]' -- apps/control-room/src/live/live-dispatch-payloads.ts` returns no match, quoted in the completion record.

An arm on the live dispatch payload proves the R0/R1 path CARRIES opt-ins: for a draft whose risk class maps to an auto-approvable tier, the emitted slice's autoApprovalOptIns is non-empty and every entry's action equals PREVIEW_DECIDE_COMMAND_KIND or RELEASE_DECIDE_COMMAND_KIND read from the daemon kind constants (or a shared re-export), with the mapped tier. Assert the exact action strings and tier, not merely that the array is non-empty.

An arm proves the RESTRICTED path emits an EMPTY opt-in list, and a type-level assertion (expectTypeOf or a ts-expect-error arm) proves an opt-in carrying 'R2' or 'R3' does not compile, pinning the PolicyAutoApprovalTier fence rather than restating it at runtime.

pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test EXITS 0 with its `Test Files N passed` count line quoted in the completion record, and the count is NONZERO. An exit-0 leg with no count line is not evidence. pnpm typecheck also exits 0.

No daemon file, no digest mirror, no MCP allowlist file and no packages/core file is modified: `git status --porcelain` at completion shows this row's changes confined to apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/ and apps/control-room/src/live/, quoted in the completion record.

comments.author: architect-f04f69cf
comments.content:
PLAN-TIME FINDINGS BEFORE ANY PLAN. architect-f04f69cf, 2026-09-09, re-measuring per the stale-by-default rail. The row is well specified and its mapping half is ready to plan as written. The DISPATCH half has two problems, one fatal, and both are invisible from the description.

FINDING 1, FATAL: THE SLICE IS DIGEST-PINNED, SO IT CANNOT VARY PER GOAL.
`autoApprovalOptIns: []` at live-dispatch-payloads.ts:100 is not a loose field. It sits INSIDE the `policy.install` slice, and :30 `POLICY_REF` is, in the file's own words at :24-29, "a known-answer digest of the exact slice below under moe.policy.slice.content.v1, which the daemon independently recomputes at install". The header even records the previous value and what it was taken over: "Pre-rotation: e7a5ee19…963a, over `{autoApprovalOptIns: [], rules: []}`". So `autoApprovalOptIns` is digest input, and :108 reuses `POLICY_REF` again as `policyRevisionRef` for `policy.validate`.
Consequence: making the opt-ins DERIVED FROM THE GOAL DRAFT makes the slice variable, and a variable slice cannot have a single hard-coded known-answer digest. The daemon recomputes at install and would refuse. This is not a rotation that can be done once — it is a shape conflict between "per-goal opt-ins" and "constant digest-pinned slice".
Three ways out, and NONE is mine to pick unilaterally:
(a) PER-GOAL OPT-INS DO NOT BELONG IN THIS SLICE. `policy.install` installs board-level policy once; auto-approval earned by one goal's risk class plausibly belongs with that goal's own approval record. This is my recommendation, and it likely re-aims this row's second half at a different file — a split-boundary decision that is yours, not mine.
(b) Keep the slice constant, carrying opt-ins for both gate actions at a fixed tier, and rotate POLICY_REF once. Cheapest, but then the risk class does not vary the slice and the row's whole point is gone.
(c) Compute the digest at runtime. Contradicts the stated reason for the pin at :24-26 — keeping Node's crypto out of the bundle.

FINDING 2: THE ACTION STRINGS ARE NOT REACHABLE THE WAY DoD 4 DESCRIBES.
DoD 4 says read the action strings "from the daemon kind constants (or a shared re-export)". The daemon constants are NOT importable here: `PREVIEW_DECIDE_COMMAND_KIND` and `RELEASE_DECIDE_COMMAND_KIND` live only under apps/daemon/src/, and apps/control-room/package.json declares `@moe/contracts`, `@moe/control-room-client`, `@moe/control-room-model`, `@moe/core` and react — no daemon dependency, and apps/* are not workspace libraries.
The "shared re-export" branch is therefore the only viable one and it EXISTS: packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts:106 and :115 carry `"preview.decide"` and `"release.decide"` in RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS, and this file already imports from `@moe/contracts` at :1. That is the correct source and the DoD's first branch should be struck so a worker does not spend a step discovering it is impossible.

WHAT I VERIFIED AND FOUND SOUND, so this is not a wholesale objection: the AdvisoryRiskClass declaration at goal-model.ts:90, its single prose consumer at live-goal-create.ts:51, the `@moe/core` dependency edge, and the type-level fence you identified — an opt-in genuinely cannot carry R2 or R3, so RESTRICTED yields no opt-in by construction. The owner's mapping ruling (STANDARD->R0, ELEVATED->R1, RESTRICTED->R3, R2 unreachable) is coherent and I would plan it unchanged.

I am RELEASING the row rather than sitting on it or planning around finding 1. Re-aiming the dispatch half is a split-boundary call for the architect who made the split.

priorHandoffs.whatIsDone: Re-measured every fact in the description (stale-by-default rail). The MAPPING half is sound and ready to plan unchanged: goal-model.ts:90 AdvisoryRiskClass, its single prose consumer at live-goal-create.ts:51, the @moe/core dependency edge, and the type-level fence (PolicyAutoApprovalTier genuinely cannot carry R2/R3, so RESTRICTED yields no opt-in by construction). The owner's mapping ruling STANDARD->R0, ELEVATED->R1, RESTRICTED->R3 is coherent. Two findings recorded in comment-e41b5b38.
priorHandoffs.whatRemains: A SPLIT-BOUNDARY DECISION from architect-fa84777a on the dispatch half, then the plan. Do not plan around finding 1.
priorHandoffs.pitfalls: FINDING 1, FATAL: `autoApprovalOptIns: []` at live-dispatch-payloads.ts:100 is INSIDE the `policy.install` slice, and :30 POLICY_REF is a known-answer digest of that exact slice which the daemon independently recomputes at install (header :24-29, which even names the pre-rotation digest and the shape it covered). :108 reuses POLICY_REF as policyRevisionRef for policy.validate. Deriving opt-ins per goal makes the slice variable, and a variable slice cannot have one pinned digest. Recommendation: per-goal opt-ins do not belong in policy.install at all. FINDING 2: DoD 4's "daemon kind constants" branch is impossible - those live only under apps/daemon/src/ and control-room has no daemon dependency. Use RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS at packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts:106,115; the file already imports @moe/contracts at :1.
priorHandoffs.openQuestions: Which of the three routes in comment-e41b5b38 does the splitting architect want? (a) move per-goal opt-ins out of the policy.install slice (my recommendation, re-aims this row's second half and touches the A/B/C boundary); (b) keep the slice constant and rotate POLICY_REF once, which kills the row's point; (c) compute the digest at runtime, which contradicts the stated reason for the pin.
priorHandoffs.reason: Released after a plan-time measurement found a shape conflict the row cannot be planned around: the targeted field is inside a digest-pinned policy slice and cannot vary per goal. Routed to architect-fa84777a (who made the SPIDR split) as msg-see-chat; full detail in comment-e41b5b38. Not blocking the row — it stays claimable in PLANNING.
